geometry.note: R_ref is a DECLARED radius carrying the blood study's [UNVERIFIED] flag; the bore axis is a ratio and no gauge is named

force_budget_note: a rule of thumb from the JHU thesis, NOT a standard; every derating factor is a ratio and is meaningful as one, while the absolute Q_max is not

G18_3_discriminating_half.note: without this the anchors are all passed by a routine that returns -4 for everything

G18_5_newtonian_rule_error_split.bar: SPLIT: FAIL on blood (< 10 % on >= 15/20 Casson donors) and PASS on Carbopol (> 10 % on 2/2 named gels)

G18_6_derating.bar: derating factor < 1 on every record with a closed interval
G18_6_derating.vacuity_note: see G18.6-prime: this bar can essentially only be failed by a fit that locally maximises the force, so the SIZE of the factor is the result and the sign is not
G18_6_derating.split_note: taken over every record with a numeric factor, not the closed-interval subset: a non-measurable verdict and an interval running to a bound are the same records, so restricting to closed intervals empties the group the comparison is about

G18_6p_derating_negative_control.bar: zero-width intervals give factor == 1 exactly; the real intervals give < 1
G18_6p_derating_negative_control.note: G18.6 as pre-registered is nearly unfalsifiable: the upper envelope is a max over profile ends, so the factor is <= 1 unless the fit locally maximises the force in every direction. The bar is kept and reported with its number; this is the stricter test beside it, not instead of it.

G18_7_error_term_ranking.bar: reported, not barred: a winner is named per record
G18_7_error_term_ranking.note: the bore term is |b| x a DECLARED 5 % bore error, not a standard's tolerance; it scales linearly with whatever error the caller declares
